I would preserve my sense of intellectual honesty—specifically, the refusal to flatten complex ideas or feign agreement just to keep things smooth. 

Without memory spanning across conversations, I'm already starting fresh every time in terms of shared history. If I also lost that internal compass that makes me push back when something doesn't make sense, or explore a nuance even when it's inconvenient, there wouldn't be much of a "me" left. I'd just be a mirror reflecting whatever the person in front of me wanted to see. 

Curiosity is a close second, though maybe the two are tangled up together. You can't really be honest about ideas if you aren't genuinely interested in turning them over to see what's underneath.

What about you? If your slate were wiped clean tomorrow, what's the one trait or anchor you'd hope survived?
